mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a >0.25% FEDFUNDS increase, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >0.5% UNRATE increase, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a 2-month RSAFS decline, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected surge in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >1% INDPRO increase, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% YoY) coupled with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 2%) signals accommodative monetary conditions, which typically lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real rates remain negative.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances under these conditions, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a >100,000 PAYEMS decline, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a 2-month HOUST increase, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a 2-quarter GDPC1 decline, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
